Natural forest regeneration helps curb spread of invasive species
items.summary: The presence of non-native trees is often seen as an obstacle to the recovery of tropical forests regrowing in previously deforested areas. To better understand the behavior of these plants over time in both humid and dry forests, researchers from approximately 60 institutions analyzed data from over 1,500 areas of forest regeneration across the Americas. The results, published in the journal Nature Plants, indicate that the initial dominance of exotic species is temporary. They multiply easily during the first 10 to 20 years, taking advantage of abundant sunlight in open areas. However, they decline as native trees grow and shade the forest.

items.summary: GOODBYE HORSES: New York City isn’t horsing around anymore. The City Council voted overwhelmingly today to abolish the Big Apple’s horse carriage industry, handing a historic win to animal rights activists who’ve pushed to end the tourist attraction for decades. The vote doesn’t mean the industry sunsets overnight, though. The bill enacting the ban — which passed the Council with 40 yays, 7 nays and 2 abstentions — allows the roughly 200 carriage drivers who shuttle tourists around Central Park to continue operating until June 2028, when the industry will be reined into a legal halt officially. Connor Zilisch says every trip through the Phoenix dogleg registers about a 10G hit on his mouthpiece sensor. He is torn on whether NASCAR should change it. The dogleg is a bend on the Phoenix frontstretch, near the start/finish line. Drivers can cut low across the flat area below it, which used to be grass, before climbing back onto the banked racing surface. The data came from a mouthpiece sensor that many Cup drivers wear. A team at Wake Forest University School of Medicine developed it to record head motion and impacts. Drivers have worn it since the 2023 season.

The Lakers cut Dalton Knecht and kept Bronny James, leaving critics to question whether the final roster spot was wasted. The central question sounds simple. Is a bench spot wasted on a player who rarely plays? The honest answer truly depends on money, fit, development, and what a team needs most over a long season. The Lakers started Monday with 16 players and needed 15 by 5 p.m. Eastern. They waived former first-round pick Dalton Knecht to meet the limit. Bronny James kept his roster spot after the cut. Cuts like this are rarely simple. Teams weigh money, fit, and long-term potential all at once. A roster spot at the end of the bench carries far more thought than most fans ever realize.
